Satellite images showed most of the warship capsized and submerged, with only its bow remaining above water. Smoke could be seen rising from the ship's superstructure, and debris was scattered along the pier. Ten people, including Russian and Libyan nationals, suffered minor injuries in the attack and were receiving treatment in Benghazi, medical sources told Reuters. The warship had stopped at the port to refuel and resupply while returning to Russia under a maritime cooperation agreement with Libya's eastern-based government, officials said in a statement. items.summary_original: Armenia is set to launch a U.S.-backed transportation and energy project along Iran's northern border Monday, despite warnings from a senior Iranian official that Tehran would "break their legs" if President Donald Trump and his allies crossed the Islamic Republic's "red line." Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan confirmed that the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project would launch Monday, advancing the plan to connect mainland Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave through southern Armenia and establish energy links with Turkey and Azerbaijan, Turkish media reported, citing Interfax. The project, a centerpiece of a U.S.-brokered peace initiative between Armenia and Azerbaijan, would also expand American economic involvement in the South Caucasus, where Iran has warned against any development it believes could threaten its security or regional influence. TRUMP'S FIRST IRAN WAR ESCALATION POST-MIDTERM LOSSES SEEKS TO CHOKE OFF TEHRAN’S TRADE The corridor has also gained strategic significance amid the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, as Tehran seeks to secure its northern trade routes and limit the U.S. security presence near its borders while Washington maintains its naval blockade and Task Force Iron Gate focuses on Iran's borders. Speaking at the DigiTec 2026 technology conference in Yerevan, Pashinyan said the new TRIPP initiative, also known as the "Trump Corridor," would strengthen Armenia's regional energy connections, according to Interfax .
